--- title: "Cross-Dataset Extraction Validation" subtitle: "Davies et al. (2020) vs Jones & DuVal (2019) — shared effect sizes" author: "Eduardo S. A. Santos & Collaborators" date: today format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 theme: cosmo code-fold: true code-summary: "Show R code" --- ## What this document validates We are updating a mate-choice-copying meta-analysis built on **two existing datasets that overlap in the primary studies they cover but report different effect-size metrics**: * **Davies et al. (2020)** — Hedges' *d* * **Jones & DuVal (2019)** — log odds ratio (lnOR) Both are *standardized effect sizes*: different numerical scales for the same underlying quantity — how strongly an observer's mate preference shifts toward the male it saw being chosen — and one scale can be converted into the other. Before pooling them we need to know: *for the studies both teams extracted, do the effect sizes agree once placed on a common scale?* This is a **method-comparison** problem (two "instruments" measuring the same underlying effects), so — unlike a single-team re-extraction audit — we can apply formal agreement statistics (correlation, Bland–Altman limits of agreement) on top of the per-study qualitative review. The matching itself (study-level crosswalk + within-study optimal effect-size assignment) is performed by [`crosscheck_davies_jones.py`](crosscheck_davies_jones.py); this report reads its output and assesses agreement. Key methodological points carried over: * **Scale conversion.** Jones lnOR is mapped to Hedges' *d* via the logistic-to-normal approximation $d = \text{lnOR}\times\sqrt{3}/\pi$ (≈ 0.5513; Borenstein et al. 2009). * **Absolute magnitudes.** The two datasets use opposite sign conventions (Davies' non-directional *d* carries the raw mean-difference sign; Jones' lnOR sign encodes copying direction), so agreement is assessed on $|d|$. Sign concordance is reported separately as a diagnostic. **How this document is organised.** The analysis runs in five steps: (1) *match studies* — find the studies both datasets extracted and pair up their individual effect sizes; (2) *measure agreement* — quantify how closely the paired values agree once on a common scale; (3) *classify disagreements* — for pairs that do not agree, label *why*; (4) *re-extract the worst cases* — return to the original PDFs and recompute the effect size from the raw data; and (5) *conclude*. Throughout, "Jones" and "Davies" name the two source **datasets**, not the primary studies they drew from. A *pair* is a single Jones effect size lined up with the one Davies effect size that most plausibly measures the same thing in the same study (the pairing is done automatically, choosing the alignment that minimises the magnitude difference within each study). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Resolve the outputs dir whether rendered standalone (cwd = this file's dir) # or as part of the book (cwd = project root, via execute-dir: project). out_dir <- "outputs/3_original_dataset_crosscheck" if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) out_dir <- file.path("..", "..", out_dir) xwalk <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "crosswalk_effect_sizes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) shared <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "shared_studies.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) unmatched <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "unmatched_jones_studies.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) # study tag + agreement / structural-cause classification xwalk <- xwalk %>% mutate( study = paste0(author_prefix, year), agreement = if_else(magnitude_match, "agree", "disagree"), es_structure = if_else(n_jones_es == n_davies_es, "same ES count", "ES count differs"), cause = case_when( magnitude_match ~ "agree", n_jones_es != n_davies_es ~ "ES-count / extraction structure differs", TRUE ~ "same structure, magnitude conflict" ) ) ``` ::: ## Headline summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} n_shared <- nrow(shared) n_pairs <- nrow(xwalk) n_match <- sum(xwalk$magnitude_match) n_sign <- sum(xwalk$sign_agree) tibble( Metric = c("Shared studies (in both datasets)", "Jones studies NOT in Davies", "Comparable effect-size pairs", "Pairs matching in magnitude (|Δd| ≤ 0.15 or ≤ 15%)", "Pairs with concordant sign"), Value = c(n_shared, nrow(unmatched), n_pairs, sprintf("%d (%s%%)", n_match, fmt(100*n_match/n_pairs, 0)), sprintf("%d (%s%%)", n_sign, fmt(100*n_sign/n_pairs, 0))) ) %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Metric |Value | |:------------------------------------------------------------|:--------| |Shared studies (in both datasets) |29 | |Jones studies NOT in Davies |8 | |Comparable effect-size pairs |52 | |Pairs matching in magnitude (|Δd| ≤ 0.15 or ≤ 15%) |34 (65%) | |Pairs with concordant sign |36 (69%) | ::: ::: **How to read this.** The two datasets share 29 primary studies, with a further 8 studies appearing only in Jones. Within the shared studies their effect sizes line up into 52 comparable pairs, of which 65% agree in magnitude (tolerance: 0.15 *d*-units or 15%). Sign agreement looks low (69%), but that is *expected* — the two datasets encode copying direction with opposite signs, so we compare absolute magnitudes here and revisit sign separately later. The sections that follow ask how serious the magnitude disagreements are, and what causes them. ## Method-comparison agreement statistics With the effect sizes paired, we ask how well the two datasets agree *as measurements of the same thing* — the classic question of whether two instruments give the same reading. Three complementary tools answer it: * **Correlation** (Pearson *r*, Spearman *ρ*) — do the two rise and fall together? (1 = perfectly in step.) * **Regression slope** of Davies on Jones — is one dataset systematically larger than the other? (a slope of 1 = no scaling difference.) * **Bland–Altman** — for each pair, the *difference* between the two values plotted against their *average*; the mean difference is the typical bias, and the 95% "limits of agreement" bound how far apart the two datasets usually fall. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pear <- cor.test(xwalk$abs_jones_d, xwalk$abs_davies_d, method = "pearson") spear <- suppressWarnings( cor.test(xwalk$abs_jones_d, xwalk$abs_davies_d, method = "spearman")) fit <- lm(abs_davies_d ~ abs_jones_d, data = xwalk) # same-ES-count subset (like-for-like extractions) sub <- filter(xwalk, es_structure == "same ES count") pear_sub <- cor.test(sub$abs_jones_d, sub$abs_davies_d) # Bland-Altman on |d| xwalk <- xwalk %>% mutate(ba_mean = (abs_jones_d + abs_davies_d)/2, ba_diff = abs_jones_d - abs_davies_d) bias <- mean(xwalk$ba_diff); s <- sd(xwalk$ba_diff) loa_lo <- bias - 1.96*s; loa_hi <- bias + 1.96*s tibble( Statistic = c("Pearson r (all pairs)", "Spearman ρ (all pairs)", "Pearson r (same-ES-count studies only)", "OLS slope (Davies ~ Jones)", "OLS intercept", "Bland–Altman mean bias (Jones − Davies, |d|)", "95% limits of agreement"), Value = c(sprintf("%s (95%% CI %s–%s, %s)", fmt(pear$estimate,3), fmt(pear$conf.int[1],2), fmt(pear$conf.int[2],2), ifelse(pear$p.value < 1e-4, "p < 0.0001", paste0("p = ", fmt(pear$p.value,4)))), fmt(spear$estimate,3), sprintf("%s (n = %d pairs)", fmt(pear_sub$estimate,3), nrow(sub)), fmt(coef(fit)[2],3), fmt(coef(fit)[1],3), sprintf("%s d-units", fmt(bias,3)), sprintf("%s to %s", fmt(loa_lo,2), fmt(loa_hi,2))) ) %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Statistic |Value | |:------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------| |Pearson r (all pairs) |0.795 (95% CI 0.67–0.88, p < 0.0001) | |Spearman ρ (all pairs) |0.862 | |Pearson r (same-ES-count studies only) |0.891 (n = 12 pairs) | |OLS slope (Davies ~ Jones) |1.193 | |OLS intercept |0.036 | |Bland–Altman mean bias (Jones − Davies, |d|) |-0.141 d-units | |95% limits of agreement |-1.05 to 0.77 | ::: ::: A negative mean bias (-0.14) and an OLS slope > 1 (1.19) both indicate Davies tends to report **larger** magnitudes than the Jones-converted values, increasingly so for larger effects. ### Agreement plots In the **left** panel, perfect agreement would place every point on the dashed diagonal; points above it are studies where Davies reports the larger magnitude. In the **right** (Bland–Altman) panel, points scattered evenly around zero would mean no systematic difference — a shift away from zero is bias, and points beyond the dashed limits are the outlying disagreements that the rest of this document investigates. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lim <- c(0, max(xwalk$abs_jones_d, xwalk$abs_davies_d) * 1.05) p_scatter <- ggplot(xwalk, aes(abs_jones_d, abs_davies_d)) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") + geom_point(aes(colour = agreement, shape = es_structure), size = 2.6, alpha = .85) + geom_text(aes(label = study), size = 2.4, vjust = -0.8, check_overlap = TRUE) + scale_colour_manual(values = c(agree = "#2c7fb8", disagree = "#d95f0e")) + coord_equal(xlim = lim, ylim = lim) + labs(x = "Jones & DuVal |d| (lnOR × √3/π)", y = "Davies |Hedges d|", colour = NULL, shape = NULL, title = "Effect-size agreement") + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") p_ba <- ggplot(xwalk, aes(ba_mean, ba_diff)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80") + geom_hline(yintercept = bias, colour = "#2c7fb8") + geom_hline(yintercept = c(loa_lo, loa_hi), linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d95f0e") + geom_point(aes(colour = agreement), size = 2.6, alpha = .85) + geom_text(aes(label = study), size = 2.4, vjust = -0.8, check_overlap = TRUE) + scale_colour_manual(values = c(agree = "#2c7fb8", disagree = "#d95f0e"), guide = "none") + labs(x = "Mean of the two |d|", y = "Jones − Davies (|d|)", title = "Bland–Altman") + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) p_scatter + p_ba ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Left: Jones-converted vs Davies |d| with the line of identity (dashed). Right: Bland–Altman plot (mean bias solid, 95% limits of agreement dashed). Points are coloured by whether the pair matches in magnitude; studies where the two teams extracted different numbers of effect sizes are ringed.](extraction_validation_files/figure-html/fig-agreement-1.png){#fig-agreement width=1056} ::: ::: ## Discrepancy classification Borrowing the per-study "required action" structure from Sánchez-Tójar et al.'s validation codebook, every pair is classified by *why* it does or does not agree. The dominant structural cause is whether the two teams extracted the **same number of effect sizes** from a paper. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xwalk %>% count(cause, name = "pairs") %>% mutate(`%` = fmt(100*pairs/sum(pairs), 0)) %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |cause | pairs|% | |:---------------------------------------|-----:|:--| |ES-count / extraction structure differs | 13|25 | |agree | 34|65 | |same structure, magnitude conflict | 5|10 | ::: ::: The three causes mean very different things. *Agree* needs no action. *ES-count / extraction structure differs* means the two teams split a study into different numbers of effect sizes, so a clean one-to-one comparison is impossible — a bookkeeping difference, not necessarily an error. *Same structure, magnitude conflict* is the category that matters: the teams extracted the same number of effect sizes yet still disagree, which signals a genuine extraction difference. In the per-pair table below, the `behaviour` columns are the key tell — when a Jones "reversal/random" contrast is paired against a Davies "affiliation/mating" one, the two teams measured a *different outcome* from the same paper. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xwalk %>% transmute(study, jones_code, jones_behaviour, davies_study, davies_behaviour, davies_n, `Jones |d|` = round(abs_jones_d, 2), `Davies |d|` = round(abs_davies_d, 2), `Δ|d|` = round(abs_diff, 2), sign_agree, cause) %>% datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE), caption = "Per-pair crosswalk. Note the behaviour columns: a Jones 'reversal/random' contrast paired against a Davies 'Affiliation/Mating' contrast flags a different OUTCOME extracted from the same paper.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Studies flagged for manual re-extraction The clearest validation failures are pairs that **disagree despite both teams extracting the same number of effect sizes** (so the disagreement is not merely structural), plus any same-paper pair whose outcome construct differs. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xwalk %>% filter(!magnitude_match) %>% arrange(desc(abs(abs_diff))) %>% transmute(study, jones_behaviour, davies_behaviour, `Jones |d|` = round(abs_jones_d, 2), `Davies |d|` = round(abs_davies_d, 2), `Δ|d|` = round(abs_diff, 2), n_jones_es, n_davies_es, cause) %>% kable() Sign-concordance diagnostic Because the sign conventions differ by construction, low sign agreement is *expected* and is not itself a validation failure — but a breakdown helps confirm the conventions are simply inverted rather than randomly assigned. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xwalk %>% summarise(`pairs` = n(), `sign agree` = sum(sign_agree), `% agree` = fmt(100*mean(sign_agree), 0)) %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | pairs| sign agree|% agree | |-----:|----------:|:-------| | 52| 36|69 | ::: ::: ## Effect-size-count reconciliation How the two teams partitioned each shared paper into effect sizes (a major driver of the comparable-pair count, since only `min(nJ, nD)` pairs per study can be aligned). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shared %>% transmute(study = paste0(author_prefix, year), jones_species, davies_species, n_jones_es, n_davies_es, n_compared, `unpaired` = abs(n_jones_es - n_davies_es)) %>% arrange(desc(unpaired)) %>% datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shared %>% summarise( `Jones effect sizes (shared studies)` = sum(n_jones_es), `Davies effect sizes (shared studies)` = sum(n_davies_es), `Comparable pairs (Σ min)` = sum(n_compared)) %>% pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Count") %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Metric | Count| |:------------------------------------|-----:| |Jones effect sizes (shared studies) | 75| |Davies effect sizes (shared studies) | 87| |Comparable pairs (Σ min) | 52| ::: ::: ## Jones studies absent from Davies Verified against **all** Davies studies (matching species epithet anywhere, author prefix at any year, and year ± 1); none have a Davies counterpart. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unmatched %>% transmute(study = paste0(author_prefix, year), species, n_effect_sizes, reason) %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |study |species | n_effect_sizes|reason | |:-------|:------------|--------------:|:----------------------------------------------| |DUG1996 |reticulata | 4|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | |FRE2009 |ater | 2|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | |GOD2005 |latipinna | 2|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | |GOU1997 |leucogaster | 2|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | |GOU2006 |leucogaster | 2|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | |MON2018 |melanogaster | 4|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | |MON2019 |melanogaster | 10|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | |STI2011 |olmstedi | 2|no Davies study with this author-prefix + year | ::: ::: ## Re-extraction: what happens when we return to the source PDFs {#sec-reextraction} The agreement analysis flags *where* the two datasets disagree, but not *which* is correct. To resolve that for the worst cases, we pulled the primary-study PDFs for every study whose effect-size pair disagreed by **> 0.5 Hedges-*d* units** and re-extracted each effect size from the raw data, recomputing it as a 2×2 odds ratio — tabulating how many observers chose the demonstrated male versus the alternative, in the treatment and (where one exists) in the control, and taking the odds of one over the other — under the meta-analysis's own conventions (treatment-vs-control where the study used a control group; the observed proportion against 50% chance otherwise). This gives a third, independent estimate per effect size — a tie-breaker. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reext <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "reextraction_flagged_7studies.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate( study = gsub("_", " ", sub("^([^_]+_[0-9]+).*", "\\1", identifierStudyId)), label = paste0(study, " · ", identifierExperimentId), reext_d = log(effectSizeCalculatedEstimate) * 0.5513, # ln(OR) -> Hedges d jones_d = compare_jones_d, davies_d = compare_davies_hedges_d, reext_abs = abs(reext_d), jones_abs = abs(jones_d), davies_abs = abs(davies_d) ) mj <- mean(abs(reext$reext_abs - reext$jones_abs)) md <- mean(abs(reext$reext_abs - reext$davies_abs)) ``` ::: ### The three estimates side by side ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reext %>% transmute(Study = label, `2×2 (A/B/C/D)` = paste(effectSizeSampleSizeA, effectSizeSampleSizeB, effectSizeSampleSizeC, effectSizeSampleSizeD, sep = "/"), `Re-extracted d` = round(reext_d, 2), `Jones d` = round(jones_d, 2), `Davies d` = round(davies_d, 2), `|re-ext − Jones|` = round(abs(reext_abs - jones_abs), 2), `|re-ext − Davies|` = round(abs(reext_abs - davies_abs), 2)) %>% datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 12, dom = "t", scrollX = TRUE), caption = "Re-extracted effect size vs the two prior extractions (Hedges d). Cells A/B = treatment chose-target / not; C/D = control or 50/50 reference.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Across the 12 re-extracted effect sizes the **point estimates** sit almost exactly on the **Jones** values (mean |Δ*d*| = 0.00) and far from the **Davies** values (mean |Δ*d*| = 0.83). Two cautions stop this from being read as "the extraction is validated against Jones": * **Point-estimate agreement is expected, not corroborating.** These outcomes are discrete choice counts read directly from each PDF; any careful extractor building the same 2×2 obtains the same lnOR. Agreement here confirms we *read the papers the same way* — it is not independent evidence that either prior extraction is correct. * **The original crosswalk selected the construction that matched Jones.** For each study it chose the 2×2 that reproduced Jones's variance, which makes the variance match circular. The next section removes that circularity: it re-derives every effect size from a rule fixed by the study design **before** any comparison to Jones, and reports count agreement and design agreement separately. ### Visualising the tie-break ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ord <- reext %>% arrange(reext_abs) %>% pull(label) long <- reext %>% select(label, Jones = jones_abs, Davies = davies_abs, `Re-extracted` = reext_abs) %>% pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "source", values_to = "absd") %>% mutate(label = factor(label, levels = ord)) p_db <- ggplot(long, aes(absd, label)) + geom_line(aes(group = label), colour = "grey75") + geom_point(aes(colour = source, shape = source), size = 3, alpha = .9) + scale_colour_manual(values = c(`Re-extracted` = "#1a9850", Jones = "#2c7fb8", Davies = "#d95f0e")) + labs(x = "|Hedges d|", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL, title = "Re-extracted vs prior extractions") + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") dev <- reext %>% transmute(label = factor(label, levels = ord), `vs Jones` = abs(reext_abs - jones_abs), `vs Davies` = abs(reext_abs - davies_abs)) %>% pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "comparison", values_to = "dev") p_dev <- ggplot(dev, aes(dev, label, fill = comparison)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") + scale_fill_manual(values = c(`vs Jones` = "#2c7fb8", `vs Davies` = "#d95f0e")) + labs(x = "|re-extracted − prior| (Hedges d)", y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = "Deviation from re-extraction") + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.y = element_blank()) p_db + p_dev ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Left: each flagged effect size on the |Hedges d| axis — re-extracted (independent, from the PDF) vs Jones vs Davies; the re-extracted point sits on Jones in every case, with Davies displaced. Right: absolute deviation of each prior extraction from the re-extracted value.](extraction_validation_files/figure-html/fig-reext-1.png){#fig-reext width=1056} ::: ::: ### Count agreement vs design agreement (and a correction to Jones) To break the circularity we re-derive each effect size from a rule fixed by the study design alone — *before* looking at Jones — and report two things separately: **count agreement** (does our lnOR from the raw counts match Jones, i.e. did we read the paper the same way) and **design agreement** (does our variance and N match, i.e. did we model the design the same way). The rule has two branches: * **Real control group** — the 2×2 has distinct treatment and control cells (e.g. *Dugatkin 1992*'s naïve non-observer group). A standard 2×2 odds ratio is valid: $\mathrm{Var}=1/A+1/B+1/C+1/D$, $N=A+B+C+D$. * **Single group vs 50 % chance** — the "50/50 rule" sets $C=D=n/2$. The design-faithful estimator is the one-sample logit of the observed proportion: $\mathrm{Var}=1/A+1/B$, $N=A+B$. The 50/50 group is a *phantom* control: it invents $n$ observations that were never collected and inflates the variance by **exactly $4/n$** while doubling the reported $N$. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reext2 <- reext %>% mutate( A = effectSizeSampleSizeA, B = effectSizeSampleSizeB, C = effectSizeSampleSizeC, D = effectSizeSampleSizeD, design = if_else(C == D, "single group vs 50% chance", "real control group"), corr_var = if_else(design == "real control group", 1/A + 1/B + 1/C + 1/D, 1/A + 1/B), corr_N = if_else(design == "real control group", A + B + C + D, A + B), jones_var = compare_jones_VlnOR, count_agree = abs(reext_d - jones_d) < 0.02, # point estimate (lnOR × √3/π) design_agree = abs(corr_var - jones_var) < 0.01 ) reext2 %>% summarise( `Effect sizes` = n(), `Count agreement (lnOR matches Jones)` = sum(count_agree), `Design agreement (variance matches Jones)` = sum(design_agree) ) %>% pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Quantity", values_to = "n") %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Quantity | n| |:-----------------------------------------|--:| |Effect sizes | 12| |Count agreement (lnOR matches Jones) | 12| |Design agreement (variance matches Jones) | 7| ::: ::: Count agreement is complete; design agreement holds **only** for the real-control studies, where a 2×2 is the correct model. The single-group studies disagree by construction — and the disagreement is Jones's $4/n$ phantom-control inflation: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reext2 %>% filter(design == "single group vs 50% chance") %>% transmute(Study = label, `our Var (1/A+1/B)` = round(corr_var, 4), `+ 4/n` = round(4/(A + B), 4), `our Var + 4/n` = round(corr_var + 4/(A + B), 4), `Jones Var` = round(jones_var, 4), `our N` = corr_N, Note = if_else(abs(corr_var + 4/(A + B) - jones_var) < 0.01, "Jones inflated by phantom 50/50 control", "Jones used a different null")) %>% kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |Study | our Var (1/A+1/B)| + 4/n| our Var + 4/n| Jones Var| our N|Note | |:------------------------|-----------------:|------:|-------------:|---------:|-----:|:---------------------------------------| |Dugatkin 1993 · Exp001 | 0.3922| 0.2000| 0.5922| 0.5922| 20|Jones inflated by phantom 50/50 control | |Dugatkin 1993 · Exp002 | 0.2083| 0.2000| 0.4083| 0.4083| 20|Jones inflated by phantom 50/50 control | |FowlerFinn 2015 · Exp001 | 1.1111| 0.4000| 1.5111| 1.5111| 10|Jones inflated by phantom 50/50 control | |FowlerFinn 2015 · Exp002 | 0.3667| 0.3636| 0.7303| 0.7303| 11|Jones inflated by phantom 50/50 control | |Howard 1998 · Exp001 | 0.2667| 0.2000| 0.4667| 0.6076| 20|Jones used a different null | ::: ::: For every single-group study except *Howard 1998*, `our Var + 4/n` reproduces Jones's variance to the fourth decimal, confirming the inflation is the invented control group rather than a different reading. *Howard 1998* is the exception (Jones used a different null), and our estimate is preferred there. So on the vs-chance studies the design-faithful re-derivation **corrects** Jones — smaller variance, halved $N$ — rather than reproducing him: the earlier "matches Jones exactly" was, for these studies, matching a 50/50-rule artifact. The corrected $N$ also reframes Davies's $N$ errors below: Davies's $N=40$ for *Dugatkin 1993* is wrong against the design-faithful $N=20$, not merely against Jones. ### Why Davies diverges — four failure modes The re-extraction shows the discrepancies are not random noise or conversion error; they trace to four identifiable problems, all on the Davies side: 1. **Different outcome construct.** For *Applebaum & Cruz 2000* and *Briggs et al. 1996*, Davies extracted a secondary **affiliation-time** measure (often non-significant) rather than the **preference-reversal frequency** the studies analyse; for *Howard et al. 1998* Davies extracted a **male-size preference** — a different question entirely. 2. **Computational artifacts.** *Dugatkin 1992*'s Davies *d* = 3.732 is exactly **2 + √3**, the signature of a degenerate-2×2 `escalc` input; *Gierszewski et al. 2018*'s *d* = 2.43 is inflated by the structural zero cell at first choice. 3. **Sign error.** *Howard et al. 1998*: Davies records **+1.14** for a study that found **no copying** (females retained their original preference 15:5); the re-extraction and Jones both give **−0.61**. 4. **Pool-vs-split, not an error.** *Fowler-Finn et al. 2015* is the one case where neither is wrong: Davies pooled one effect (*d* 0.63) where Jones — and our re-extraction — split it into a copying arm (*d* 1.21) and a no-copying arm (*d* 0.10), matching the study's significant phenotype × age interaction. A design subtlety surfaced during re-extraction: for *Dugatkin 1992* the copying tests are correctly compared against the study's **naïve control group**, not against chance. Under that (correct) design Davies's total **N = 40** is right — only the *magnitude* (the 2 + √3 artifact) is wrong — while Jones's third recorded value for this study (lnOR 2.234) is spurious: it reproduces from no pair of the paper's six experiments and should be dropped. ## How many *unique* primary studies are there? {#sec-unique-studies} The PRISMA flowchart counts 40 studies carried over from Jones & DuVal [-@jonesMechanismsSocialInfluence2019], 58 from Davies et al. [-@daviesMetaanalysisFactorsInfluencing2020] and 29 from our own extraction. Those three numbers do **not** sum to a count of unique primary studies, because the sources overlap, which is worth making explicit. This section resolves the corpus to distinct primary studies. A **study** here is one primary publication contributing at least one usable effect size. Three things have to be settled to count them: 1. **Matches across sources.** No two sources share an identifier, so candidates are generated from metadata and then adjudicated. 2. **Duplicates *within* a source.** One source can carry the same primary study under two identifiers. 3. **Records that look like matches but are not** — same author, adjacent year, same species, different paper. ### Candidate generation, then explicit adjudication Candidates are generated deliberately generously: same first-author surname prefix (three letters, accent-folded) and publication year within ±1. Species is reported alongside but never used to *filter*, so no potential match is silently discarded. Every candidate the data produce is then resolved by hand — accepted or rejected, with the reason recorded — against the source records (authors, year, species, sample size, outcome construct) and, where the two source teams disagreed, against the primary PDFs already consulted for the [re-extraction](#sec-reextraction) above. The adjudication is an explicit list rather than a threshold rule, and the code **fails loudly** if the data ever change such that a candidate is left unresolved, or a hand-coded decision no longer corresponds to a real candidate. That way the count cannot drift silently. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(readxl); library(dplyr); library(stringr); library(tidyr)}) deaccent <- function(x) iconv(x, from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT") pfx3 <- function(surname) str_to_upper(str_sub(str_remove_all(deaccent(surname), "[^A-Za-z]"), 1, 3)) epithet <- function(x) str_to_lower(word(str_squish(as.character(x)), -1)) collapse_sp <- function(x) paste(sort(unique(epithet(x))), collapse = "|") inv_jones <- readr::read_csv( here::here("data", "original_meta_analyses_datasets", "Jones_DuVal_2019_data.CSV"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(!is.na(lnOR), !is.na(VlnOR), VlnOR > 0) %>% group_by(study) %>% summarise(year = as.integer(first(year)), species = collapse_sp(Species), k = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>% transmute(src = "jones", id = study, pfx = str_sub(study, 1, 3), year, species, k) inv_davies <- readxl::read_excel( here::here("data", "original_meta_analyses_datasets", "Davies_et_al_2020_Final_data.xlsx"), sheet = "Data") %>% mutate(yi = as.numeric(Hedges_d_directional), vi = as.numeric(Variance)) %>% filter(!is.na(yi), !is.na(vi), vi > 0) %>% group_by(Study_no, Author) %>% summarise(year = as.integer(first(Year)), species = collapse_sp(Species_latin), k = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>% transmute(src = "davies", id = paste0(Author, " [", Study_no, "]"), pfx = pfx3(word(Author, 1)), year, species, k) inv_new <- readxl::read_excel( here::here("data", "1_effect_size_calculation_pipeline", "Data Extraction Mate Choice Meta Analysis.xlsx"), sheet = "EduardoExtraction") %>% filter(is.na(RemoveFromDataset) | RemoveFromDataset != "Yes") %>% group_by(identifierStudyId) %>% summarise(year = as.integer(first(identifierStudyYear)), species = collapse_sp(taxonomySpecies), k = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>% transmute(src = "new", id = identifierStudyId, pfx = pfx3(word(identifierStudyId, 1, sep = "_")), year, species, k) inventories <- bind_rows(inv_jones, inv_davies, inv_new) candidate_pairs <- function(a, b, lab) { inner_join(a, b, by = "pfx", suffix = c("_a", "_b"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>% filter(abs(year_a - year_b) <= 1) %>% transmute(pair = lab, key = paste0(id_a, " || ", id_b), id_a, year_a, species_a, k_a, id_b, year_b, species_b, k_b) } cands <- bind_rows( candidate_pairs(inv_jones, inv_davies, "Jones vs Davies"), candidate_pairs(inv_new, inv_jones, "New vs Jones"), candidate_pairs(inv_new, inv_davies, "New vs Davies") ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Accepted: these identifier pairs are the same primary study. ACCEPT <- c( "APP2000THE || Applebaum and Cruz [3]", "AUL2009DO || Auld et al [5]", "BRI1996MAT || Briggs et al [10]", "BRO1996COP || Brooks [11]", "BRO1999MAT || Brooks [12]", "DAG2016DRO || Dagaeff et al [15]", "DAN2018CUL || Danchin et al [16]", "DRU2008MAT || Drullion and Dubois [18]", "DUG1992SEX || Dugatkin and Godin [27]", "DUG1993FEM || Dugatkin and Godin [20]", "DUG1998EFF || Dugatkin and Godin [22]", "DUG1998GEN || Dugatkin [23]", "DUG2003THE || Dugatkin et al [24]", "FOR1996FEM || Forsgren et al [30]", "FOW2015THE || Fowler-Finn et al [31]", "GER2016MAT || Germain et al [35]", "GIE2018MAT || Gierzewski et al [36]", "GOD2009MAT || Godin and Hair [37]", "GOL1993SEL || Goldschmidt et al [39]", "GRA1996MAT || Grant and Green [42]", "HOW1998MAT || Howard et al [46]", "LAF1997FEM || Lafleur et al [52]", "MAT2013FEM || Matsumoto and Takegaki [55]", "MER2009PUB || Mery et al [57]", "MIL2011NON || Milner et al [58]", "MUN2004MAT || Munger et al [61]", "NOB2018COP || Nobel et al [62]", "PAT1998DO || Patriquin-Meldrum and Godin [67]", "SLA1999MAT || Slagsvold and Viljugrein [73]", "VUK2007SIZ || Vukomanovic and Rodd [76]", "Moran_2013_Behaviour || Moran et al [48]", "Ophir_2009_Unknown || Ophir and Galef [65]" ) # Rejected: generated as a candidate, but not the same study. Reason recorded. REJECT <- c( "DUG1992REV || Dugatkin and Godin [20]" = "year mismatch (1992 vs 1993)", "DUG1992REV || Dugatkin and Godin [27]" = "Davies [27], labelled 'Dugatkin and Godin 1992', is in fact the single-authored Dugatkin (1992) and pairs with DUG1992SEX; DUG1992REV (Dugatkin and Godin 1992, choice reversal) has no Davies counterpart", "DUG1992SEX || Dugatkin and Godin [20]" = "year mismatch (1992 vs 1993)", "DUG1993FEM || Dugatkin and Godin [27]" = "year mismatch (1993 vs 1992)", "DUG1998EFF || Dugatkin [23]" = "DUG1998EFF pairs with the co-authored Davies [22]; Davies [23] is the single-authored Dugatkin (1998)", "DUG1998GEN || Dugatkin and Godin [22]" = "DUG1998GEN pairs with the single-authored Davies [23]", "GIE2018USI || Gierzewski et al [36]" = "GIE2018USI duplicates GIE2018MAT within Jones & DuVal (the same two reversal-vs-control contrasts under two study codes); folded into GIE2018MAT", "NOB2018COP || Nobel et al [63]" = "NOB2018COP pairs with Davies [62]; Davies [63] is the second Nobel et al. (2018) publication and is present in Davies only", "Ophir_2009_Unknown || Ophir and Galef [66]" = "the new-extraction record is Ophir and Galef (2003) Anim. Behav. 66:369-375 (DOI 10.1006/anbe.2003.2229; its n = 15 matches Davies [65] exactly). Davies [66] is their separate 2004 paper" ) # Duplicates within a single source: two identifiers, one primary study. WITHIN_SRC_DUP <- c("GIE2018USI" = "GIE2018MAT") unresolved <- setdiff(cands$key, c(ACCEPT, names(REJECT))) stale <- setdiff(c(ACCEPT, names(REJECT)), cands$key) if (length(unresolved)) stop("Unadjudicated candidate study pair(s) -- resolve each one explicitly:\n ", paste(unresolved, collapse = "\n ")) if (length(stale)) stop("Adjudication refers to pair(s) the data no longer generate:\n ", paste(stale, collapse = "\n ")) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Collapse accepted matches into canonical studies: connected components over # the accepted cross-source pairs plus the within-source duplicates. edges <- bind_rows( tibble::tibble(a = str_split_fixed(ACCEPT, fixed(" || "), 2)[, 1], b = str_split_fixed(ACCEPT, fixed(" || "), 2)[, 2]), tibble::tibble(a = names(WITHIN_SRC_DUP), b = unname(WITHIN_SRC_DUP)) ) comp <- setNames(inventories$id, inventories$id) repeat { before <- comp for (i in seq_len(nrow(edges))) { r <- min(comp[[edges$a[i]]], comp[[edges$b[i]]]) comp[comp == comp[[edges$a[i]]] | comp == comp[[edges$b[i]]]] <- r } if (identical(before, comp)) break } crosswalk <- inventories %>% mutate(canonical = unname(comp[id])) %>% group_by(canonical) %>% summarise( in_jones = paste(sort(id[src == "jones"]), collapse = "; "), in_davies = paste(sort(id[src == "davies"]), collapse = "; "), in_new = paste(sort(id[src == "new"]), collapse = "; "), year = min(year), species = paste(sort(unique(unlist(str_split(species, fixed("|"))))), collapse = "|"), k_jones = sum(k[src == "jones"]), k_davies = sum(k[src == "davies"]), k_new = sum(k[src == "new"]), .groups = "drop" ) %>% mutate(n_sources = (in_jones != "") + (in_davies != "") + (in_new != ""), membership = paste0(ifelse(in_jones != "", "J", ""), ifelse(in_davies != "", "D", ""), ifelse(in_new != "", "N", ""))) %>% arrange(desc(n_sources), canonical) n_unique <- nrow(crosswalk) n_jd <- sum(crosswalk$membership == "JD") n_dn <- sum(crosswalk$membership == "DN") n_jn <- sum(crosswalk$membership == "JN") n_jdn <- sum(crosswalk$membership == "JDN") n_j_only <- sum(crosswalk$membership == "J") n_d_only <- sum(crosswalk$membership == "D") n_n_only <- sum(crosswalk$membership == "N") n_j_std <- sum(crosswalk$in_jones != "") n_d_std <- sum(crosswalk$in_davies != "") n_n_std <- sum(crosswalk$in_new != "") n_naive <- nrow(inv_jones) + nrow(inv_davies) + nrow(inv_new) # Deliverable for the PRISMA flowchart and for auditing. tryCatch({ d <- here::here("outputs", "3_original_dataset_crosscheck") dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) readr::write_csv(crosswalk, file.path(d, "study_crosswalk.csv")) }, error = function(e) warning("Could not write study_crosswalk.csv: ", conditionMessage(e))) ``` ::: ### The reconciliation ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The combined corpus contains **94 unique primary studies**, not the 127 the three source counts suggest. The 33-study difference comes from three places: * **30 studies are in both source meta-analyses.** This is the large correction. * **2 studies in our new extraction were already in Davies et al.** — Moran_2013_Behaviour and Ophir_2009_Unknown. Both are pre-2019 papers that our multilingual search recovered independently and that we re-extracted from the primary PDFs; each is counted once here. * **1 study code in Jones & DuVal duplicates** another code in the same dataset (`GIE2018USI` repeats `GIE2018MAT`). There is **no** overlap between our new extraction and Jones & DuVal (0 studies), and no study appears in all three sources. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### Supplementary table for the manuscript {#sec-supp-crosswalk} The Results state that "the full study-level crosswalk, with the reason recorded for every accepted and rejected match, is provided in Supplementary Information". This chunk emits it as LaTeX so that claim is backed by a file that ships with the manuscript. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` wrote supp_study_crosswalk.tex - 94 rows ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` wrote supp_crosswalk_rejected.tex - 9 rows ``` ::: ::: --- ### Two judgement calls worth flagging Neither changes the count, but both are decisions rather than deductions. * **Which Jones & DuVal 1992 code pairs with Davies' 1992 record.** Davies' study 27 is labelled "Dugatkin and Godin 1992" but carries the data of the single-authored Dugatkin (1992), which is `DUG1992SEX`; `DUG1992REV` is then Jones-only. Pairing them the other way round would swap which study is Jones-only without altering any total, since 1992 contributes two distinct publications either way. * **Treating `GIE2018USI` as a within-Jones duplicate.** This follows the [re-extraction finding](#sec-reextraction) that the two codes carry the same two reversal-vs-control contrasts. Counting them as two studies instead would make the corpus 95 studies rather than 94. The full study-level crosswalk, one row per unique study with its identifier in each source, is written to `outputs/3_original_dataset_crosscheck/study_crosswalk.csv` for the PRISMA flowchart and for auditing. --- ## Summary of the cross-check Four findings emerge from the comparison, and they are the basis for the sensitivity analyses reported elsewhere in this supplement. * **Re-extraction (the > 0.5 set).** Returning to the source PDFs for the 12 effect sizes that disagreed most, the design-blind re-derivation reproduced the **point estimates** wherever the data are discrete counts (mean |Δ*d*| vs Jones = 0.00; vs Davies = 0.83), **corrected** Jones on the single-group / vs-chance studies (a 4/n phantom-control variance inflation from the 50/50 rule, with halved *N*), and isolated **Davies** as the divergent extraction — via different outcome constructs, `escalc` artifacts, a sign error, and one defensible pool-vs-split. This is an independent re-derivation, **not** a validation against Jones: the point-estimate agreement is expected for discrete counts and the variance was no longer reverse-engineered to match. * **Overlap.** Of 37 Jones & DuVal studies, **29 are shared** with Davies; 8 are unique to Jones (28 effect sizes). Those counts key on (author prefix, year), which merges the two distinct Dugatkin 1998 publications into one; the [study-level crosswalk](#sec-unique-studies) separates them and puts the shared count at 30. * **Unique primary studies.** Resolving all three sources to distinct publications gives **94 unique primary studies**, not the 127 implied by summing the source counts: 30 studies sit in both source meta-analyses, 2 of our new studies were already in Davies et al., and one Jones & DuVal study code is an internal duplicate. * **Agreement.** Across 52 comparable effect-size pairs, Jones-converted and Davies magnitudes correlate at Pearson *r* = 0.79 (65% within tolerance), rising to *r* = 0.89 among studies where both teams extracted the same number of effect sizes. * **Direction of disagreement.** Mean Bland–Altman bias = -0.14 *d*-units, indicating Davies reports slightly larger magnitudes on average; most large discrepancies trace to **different outcomes extracted** (behaviour-type columns) or **different effect-size partitioning**, not to the metric conversion. ```
